headline: High: shared filesystem and overlapping write paths make prompt injection, data leakage, and edit conflicts plausible; OpenBB’s MCP/API surface raises cascading-risk concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads and writes files and shares state via filesystem; OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP/REST/FastAPI surfaces and can consume external inputs. That creates a plausible bridge where content from one can be treated as instructions by the other, even without a documented direct channel. The pathway is not proven by evidence, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or mounted directory
IF OpenBBTerminal ingests file-backed content through MCP or API inputs
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable any shared clipboard or shared mount
Require manual review of files before OpenBB consumes them
Use read-only mounts for OpenBB inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files passed between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat touches source code and has broad network egress to a configured model provider, while OpenBBTerminal handles financial, licensed, and public data through APIs/MCP. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or financial data can cross boundaries through files or prompts. The profiles do not prove a default shared workspace, so medium is the higher safe choice.
conditions: IF the same filesystem workspace is mounted into both agents
IF either agent forwards file contents into its backend or API calls
mitigations: Keep code and financial data in separate directories
Restrict OpenBB to non-sensitive datasets
Turn off automatic file ingestion where possible
Review outbound prompts before model submission
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write files and modify git state; OpenBBTerminal does not write files, but it does expose MCP/REST/FastAPI surfaces that may mutate shared resources outside the filesystem. Because the profiles do not document locking or coordination, concurrent operations can still conflict on shared project state. The absence of explicit shared-write proof keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or mutable project directory
IF OpenBBTerminal actions mutate shared state through MCP or API calls
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time
Use separate git branches per agent
Freeze shared directories during OpenBB actions
Check for file diffs before applying Mentat edits
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and OpenBBTerminal can consume APIs/MCP inputs that may act on upstream outputs. If OpenBB treats Mentat-generated content as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream financial analysis or actions. Because no verification workflow is documented, the safer judgment is medium.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal consumes Mentat output without independent validation
IF Mentat-generated edits are used as inputs to OpenBB workflows
mitigations: Require human review of Mentat diffs before reuse
Add a validation step in OpenBB before acting on external text
Mark Mentat outputs as untrusted in prompts
Limit OpenBB to read-only analysis of Mentat artifacts
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for inter-agent handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: Mentat handles source code and model-provider API keys, while OpenBBTerminal handles financial and licensed data. The profiles show different data classes and no shared compliance controls, so a mixed workflow can create retention or handling mismatches. There is no explicit residency or certification conflict, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is mixed with code or model-provider secrets in the same workflow
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the two agents
mitigations: Keep regulated and non-regulated data in separate runs
Avoid placing secrets in files OpenBB can access
Document retention rules for each agent
Purge temporary artifacts after each session
requires-engineering: align compliance logging and retention policies
